# Radial boundary variation and essential circuit blocks

This is a conditional geometric consequence of the all-active-circuit
directional condition. It does not assert that an OC extremizer belongs to
the smooth open class used here. In particular, a flat facet does not permit
arbitrary signed local boundary variations preserving convexity.

## 1. A boundary variation seen equally by every central cap

Let K be a smooth strictly convex body in R^d, d>=1, and let x_0 be an
interior point. There is a positive smooth boundary speed psi such that

    integral_(boundary K) psi dH_(d-1) = 1,
    integral_(boundary K intersect H) psi dH_(d-1) = 1/2     (1)

for every halfspace H whose boundary passes through x_0. For d>=2,
write X(omega)=x_0+r(omega)omega for radial projection from the unit sphere.
Its surface Jacobian is

    J(omega)=r(omega)^(d-1)/(omega dot n(X(omega))),

where n is the outward unit normal and omega dot n>0. Define

    psi(X(omega))=1/(|S^(d-1)| J(omega)).

Then psi dH_(d-1) is the pushforward of uniform spherical probability.
Any central halfspace corresponds to a hemisphere, whose boundary has zero
spherical measure. This proves (1). For d=1 put speed 1/2 at each endpoint;
each halfspace through an interior point contains exactly one endpoint.

For completeness, the Jacobian follows by taking the determinant of the
radial projection on each tangent space: radial projection to the unit
sphere has tangential Jacobian (omega dot n)/r^(d-1). Inverting gives J.
The speed is smooth if the body is smooth, and positive by strict interiority
and the supporting-plane inequality.

## 2. Independent realization on integer fibers

Here is an explicit ambient hypothesis under which the preceding speeds are
admissible independently at different integer fibers. Suppose

    C={w:F(w)<=0}

for a smooth coercive function F on R^(n+d), with Hessian at least cI for
some c>0 and with gradient nonzero on boundary C. Let the finite integer
fibers considered be positive. Each such fiber K_z has a smooth strictly
convex boundary: a zero continuous gradient at F(z,x)=0 would make x the
unique minimum of F(z,.) and prevent a positive fiber. Thus gradient_x F
is nonzero on its boundary.

Fix one integer z and a smooth desired speed psi on boundary K_z. Choose a
smooth compactly supported ambient function chi whose restriction there is

    chi(z,x)=|gradient_x F(z,x)| psi(x),

and whose support in the integer coordinates is within distance less than
1/3 of z. Such an extension is obtained from a tubular neighborhood of the
smooth compact fiber boundary and a bump in the integer coordinates. It
vanishes on every other integer fiber. When n=0 only the tubular extension
is needed.

For small positive and negative t, set F_t=F-t chi. The Hessian stays positive
definite because the Hessian of chi is bounded; coercivity is unchanged.
Thus C_t={F_t<=0} is a convex body. Differentiating F_t(z,x_t)=0 shows that
its continuous outward speed at the selected boundary is exactly psi. The
other integer fibers are unchanged. Finite independent speeds are realized
by adding their chi functions, with a small open box of parameter values.

Because chi is supported near a positive fiber boundary, this construction
does not introduce other nonempty integer fibers. It permits both signs;
that is the feature absent at general polyhedral or zero-curvature bodies.

## 3. Effect on every active circuit gradient

Assume the explicit hypotheses of
`candidate 6a6bd3b533ab6973`: each deepest fiber has a
unique sharp interior center, the active cap representation is compact and
uniformly differentiable in the finite family of body parameters, and the
maximum normalized depth beta is a local minimum in that open parameter
space. Let I be an essential block of deepest sites for the universal
rainbow condition, and put r=|I|.

For each z in I let delta_z be the positive radial boundary variation from
Sections 1 and 2, centered at that site's center x_z. Its total mass derivative
is one. Each cap through (z,x_z) has body-mass derivative one half, regardless
of its oblique integer coefficient: on the only moving fiber it is exactly
a central continuous halfspace. Consequently every balanced circuit gradient
g in Gamma_z has

    g(delta_z)=1/2-beta.                                    (2)

For every other deepest site w and any g in Gamma_w, each constituent cap
captures a fraction between zero and one of the nonnegative moving boundary
measure. Since circuit probabilities sum to one,

    -beta <= g(delta_z) <= 1-beta.                          (3)

These statements use the probability coefficients theta proportional to
rho/S, as in the directional note. They do not use raw circuit coefficients
rho as if they were the shape-derivative probabilities.

**Consequence 1 (singleton obstruction).** If I is a singleton and the
local radial variation is available, then beta=1/2. Indeed the robust rank
lemma gives Gamma_z={0}, and (2) gives the conclusion. In particular, a
unique deepest fiber at a local minimum in this smooth open class cannot
have normalized depth below one half.

**Consequence 2 (rank matrix and stress weights).** Choose arbitrarily
g_w in Gamma_w, w in I, and form the matrix A with entries
A_wz=g_w(delta_z). Its diagonal is 1/2-beta and every entry satisfies (3).
The rank lemma implies rank A<=r-1. More directly, the universal rainbow
condition supplies numbers p_w>=0 summing to one with sum_w p_w g_w=0.
For each column z, equations (2) and (3) give

    0 = sum_w p_w g_w(delta_z)
      >= p_z(1/2-beta) - beta(1-p_z)
       = p_z/2-beta.

Hence

    p_z<=2 beta for every z,        beta>=1/(2r).            (4)

If beta=1/(2r), every such normalized dependence has p_z=1/r, and each
off-diagonal entry with positive coefficient must attain -beta. Thus every
cap in the positively weighted circuit at w captures zero of the radial
boundary measure at a different site z. This is an exact equality condition
for this conditional estimate.

The bound (4) is a local variational obstruction, not a global centerpoint
theorem. In particular, no bound r<=2^n has been proved for essential blocks
of the all-circuit condition. Nor has existence of a smooth attained minimum
with these variations been proved. Applying (4) to the flat simplex-product
extremizers would be invalid: their independent signed radial variations
need not preserve convexity.

## 4. A finite test-space version

No infinite-dimensional optimization is needed for these conclusions.
Construct delta_z for the finitely many deepest sites first, and consider
their finite smooth ambient bump parameters. Under the directional note's
hypotheses for this family, apply its universal rainbow condition and the
finite-dimensional rank lemma there. Equations (2)--(4) hold for the
resulting essential block. For the singleton conclusion it suffices that
the selected site's normalized circuit gradients vanish on its one radial
direction.

Thus the geometric content is the explicit common value 1/2-beta of all
own-site circuit gradients on one realizable direction. The missing
general step is precisely the availability of enough signed local
variations at an attained extremizer, not an assumed vanishing of mixed
quadratic moments.
